hints: Focus on what type of reaction happens when an alcohol group reacts with a carboxylic acid in acid conditions.
Count the reacting groups: propane-1,2-diol has two -OH groups, so check how many ethanoic acid molecules must join to give $\text{C}_7\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_4$.
Look for the structure where both O atoms from the diol are now part of $\text{CH}_3\text{COO-}$ ester links, keeping the 3-carbon diol backbone intact.
walkthrough:
**Identify the reaction type**

Great start, let's see what we have. An alcohol plus a carboxylic acid with acid catalyst means esterification.

$$\text{alcohol + carboxylic acid} \rightleftharpoons \text{ester + water}$$

**Count atoms to find the stoichiometry**

Propane-1,2-diol is $\text{C}_3\text{H}_8\text{O}_2$ and ethanoic acid is $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}_2$. Try one acid first:
$$\text{C}_3\text{H}_8\text{O}_2 + \text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}_2 - \text{H}_2\text{O} = \text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_3$$
That is not $\text{C}_7\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_4$, so one ester link is not enough.

**Form the diester**

Because the diol has two -OH groups, both can esterify. Using two acids and losing two waters:
$$\text{C}_3\text{H}_8\text{O}_2 + 2(\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}_2) - 2(\text{H}_2\text{O}) = \text{C}_7\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_4$$
This matches solvent Y exactly, so Y is the diester of propane-1,2-diol.

**Select the correct diester structure**

The backbone must stay as $\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH(CH}_3\text{)-}$ with each O joined to a $\text{CH}_3\text{C=O}$ group. That is $\text{CH}_3\text{COO-CH}_2\text{-CH(CH}_3\text{)-OOCCH}_3$, which is the symmetrical diethanoate structure.

options.A: Incorrect. This has one correct ethanoate link on the left ($\text{CH}_3\text{CO-O-}$) but the right side is $\text{-C(=O)-O-CH}_3$, a methyl ester of a carboxylic acid. That would require oxidising the diol to an acid first, not simple esterification with ethanoic acid.
options.B: Incorrect. This has two $\text{-C(=O)-O-CH}_3$ methyl ester groups joined by C-C bonds to the central chain. It is a dimethyl ester of a dicarboxylic acid, so it cannot be made from a diol plus ethanoic acid where the O atoms must come from the diol.
options.C: Incorrect. This is a mixed isomer with one methyl ester end and one ethanoate end. The left side shows $\text{H}_3\text{C-O-C(=O)-C}$, meaning the carbon skeleton is joined by C-C, not by the C-O ester link expected from the diol OH group.
options.D: Correct. Both -OH groups of $\text{HO-CH}_2\text{-CH(OH)-CH}_3$ have formed $\text{O-C(=O)-CH}_3$ ester links. The product is propane-1,2-diyl diethanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)OOCCH}_3$, with formula $\text{C}_7\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_4$.
